validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + SPEC: fetched the raw HTML of the currently-cited https://www.cabinet.gov.eg/News/Details/74700 directly (not just the harvested gem.wiki snippet). It is the Egyptian Cabinet's 'petroleum sector achievements during 2023' annual review (the document is threaded through with 'خلال عام 2023' / 'during 2023' framing throughout, consistent with the youm7 article's 2024-01-14 dateline). Under the section 'مشروعات خطوط نقل الزيت الخام' (crude oil transmission line projects) it states verbatim: 'تم الانتهاء من تنفيذ وتشغيل خط نقل الزيت الخام (بدر/مسطرد) بطول 23 كم وقطر 26 بوصة بهدف رفع كفاءة الشبكة وزيادة معدلات تدفيع الخام لمعامل التكرير.. هذا وبلغت تكلفته 262 مليون جنيه' = 'Completion and commissioning of the crude oil transmission line (Badr/Musturad), 23 km long and 26 inches in diameter, to raise network efficiency and increase crude delivery rates to refineries.. at a cost of EGP 262 million.' This EXPLICITLY names Badr and Musturad together and matches GEM's Length=23.00 km, Diameter=26 in, PipelineType=transmission ('نقل'), Fuel=Oil ('الزيت الخام'), Status=operating ('تم الانتهاء من تنفيذ وتشغيل' = completed and put into operation), and StartYear1=2023 (the report's own subject year) exactly. StartLocation='Badr' and EndLocation/Province='Musturad'/'Al-Qalyubia' also confirmed (Musturad is the well-known EGPC depot/refinery node in Qalyubia governorate that recurs as a hub across this roster: P7318/P7319 Musturad-Banha, P7332/P7337 Suez-Musturad, P7340 Musturad-Tanta, P7914 Musturad-Huckstep). No capacity figure is given anywhere in the source (only cost) -- GEM's blank Capacity is correct and should NOT be force-filled. CORROBORATION-COUNT CORRECTION (the actual finding): the second cited URL, the youm7 article (2024-01-14), reproduces the Badr/Musturad sentence VERBATIM, character-for-character identical to the cabinet.gov.eg text ('...بطول 23 كم وقطر 26 بوصة بهدف رفع كفاءة الشبكة وزيادة معدلات تدفيع الخام لمعامل التكرير هذا وبلغت تكلفته 262 مليون جنيه') -- it is a same-day press-summary reprint of the Cabinet's own report, not independent reporting. Per the project's standing corroboration rule, 'the same wire story republished... do NOT count' as a second independent source. So this row in fact rests on ONE strong primary government source echoed twice, not two independent sources -- tier should read medium (1 strong), not high. This does not change any value, only the confidence bookkeeping; both URLs remain valid to keep in the [ref] cells (the youm7 mirror is useful as a backup copy of the same content, just not as independent corroboration).

validity.recommendation: cross-check P7330 against P7914 (Musturad-Huckstep Oil Pipeline) -- not a merge recommendation for P7330 itself, but the coincidence should be resolved on the P7914 side
validity.researcher_notes: While scanning the 46-row roster for duplicates of P7330 I found an unlisted coincidence not on the orchestrator's watchlist: P7914 'Musturad-Huckstep Oil Pipeline' (Musturad->Cairo, status=construction) carries the IDENTICAL spec pair Length=23.0 km / Diameter=26 in as P7330's Badr->Musturad line. Different named endpoints (Badr vs. Huckstep, both plausible distinct corridors converging on the Musturad hub) and different status (operating vs. construction), so this is likely two real, separate lines rather than a straight double-count of P7330 -- but the exact match on BOTH length and diameter to two significant figures is a real coincidence worth a second look. I read (not cited) P7914's own gem.wiki page for leads: its sole citation is https://petro-mag.org/ar/Magazine/v?id=d48e45eb-4902-4efe-b07e-c2bee996c9e1 ('December/2024 edition' of a Ministry of Petroleum magazine). I fetched that URL directly: it is only a table-of-contents/cover-image landing page for the issue, with no article text -- it does not actually confirm P7914's length or diameter anywhere I could read, and I found no Musturad-Huckstep mention in it at all. So P7914's citation is markedly weaker than P7330's (which explicitly names Badr/Musturad and gives the numbers in the cabinet.gov.eg text itself). This raises the possibility that P7914's specs were carried over from P7330 (or some other Musturad line) at entry time rather than independently sourced. P7330's own data stands on its own strong, specific primary source and needs no change; the open question is whether P7914 is a genuine, independently-specified second line or a contaminated/duplicate entry -- recommend the Egypt-oil researcher re-verify P7914's own citation when that row comes up, rather than acting on it here.

summary: P7330 confirmed real, correctly classified, and accurately specified (23 km / 26 in / operating / 2023 / Badr->Musturad, Al-Qalyubia) against the Cabinet's own 2023 petroleum-sector achievements report, which names this exact line by name; corrected the corroboration tier to medium (the youm7 ref is a verbatim reprint of the same government text, not an independent second source) and flagged an unlisted spec coincidence with P7914 (Musturad-Huckstep, same 23 km/26 in) for that row's own re-verification. No UNRESOLVED items; Capacity correctly left blank (no source gives a figure).
